## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kakaṇṭakajātaka* (Ja 170) is a short birth story in the *Dukanipāta* of the Pali Jātaka collection, situated as the tenth and concluding discourse of the *Santhavavagga* [Fausböll 1879]. The verse text opens with the line *Nāyam pure onamatīti* [Fausböll 1879]. Rather than unfolding a complete narrative at this point in the collection, the commentary provides only a brief cross-reference indicating that the full tale will be made known later in the *Mahā-ummagga-jātaka* (*Idam Kakantakajātakam Mahā-ummaggajātake āvibhavissati*) [Fausböll 1879]. In the index to the Fausböll edition, this episode is also connected to the *Kakaṇṭaka-pañha* found within the *Mahā-ummagga-jātaka* [Fausböll 1897]. Manuscript variants recorded in the critical apparatus also attest to the spelling *Kakandakajātaka* [Fausböll 1879].

 However, DharmaNexus identifies significant internal Pali text reuse between the *Kakaṇṭakajātaka* (§1.4–2.4) and four passages in the sixth volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (§2384–2386) [DharmaNexus]. This algorithmic match aligns directly with the editorial and commentarial note that the narrative material of this birth is incorporated into the extensive *Mahā-ummagga-jātaka* [DharmaNexus].
